cb1.title: The Job Banner
cb1.story: Every job printout started with a banner, so the operators knew whose paper it was.
cb1.task:
Write a job called BANNER that shows these three lines:
**************
PAYROLL RUN 1
**************
cb1.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. BANNER.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.
hints: Start with IDENTIFICATION DIVISION. and PROGRAM-ID. BANNER. in column 8.
Each DISPLAY starts in column 12: DISPLAY "**************".

cb2.title: The Name Tag
cb2.story: A conference in 1962 prints name tags on the mainframe. Use fields, and MOVE.
cb2.task:
Declare NAME-TAG as PIC X(12) and BADGE-NO as PIC 9(4). MOVE "HOPPER" into NAME-TAG and 42 into BADGE-NO. Show:
NAME: HOPPER
BADGE: 0042
cb2.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. TAG.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.
hints: In the WORKING-STORAGE SECTION: 01 NAME-TAG PIC X(12). and 01 BADGE-NO PIC 9(4).
MOVE "HOPPER" TO NAME-TAG. MOVE 42 TO BADGE-NO.
DISPLAY "NAME: " NAME-TAG.

cb3.title: The Order Counter
cb3.story: A mail-order company reads its orders from cards. Count the boxes.
cb3.task:
Read three SYSIN cards with ACCEPT, each a number of boxes, into a PIC 9(3) field. ADD each one to a total that starts at zero, and show:
BOXES TODAY: 042
cb3.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. ORDERS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.
hints: 01 BOXES PIC 9(3). and 01 TOTAL PIC 9(3) VALUE ZERO.
ACCEPT BOXES. ADD BOXES TO TOTAL. three times.
DISPLAY "BOXES TODAY: " TOTAL.

cbc1-project.title: The Bank Greeting
cbc1-project.story: 1971: the bank's mainframe greets every customer at the counter terminal. Build the job that does it.
cbc1-project.task:
Read the customer's name (PIC X(10)) and account number (PIC 9(6)) from two SYSIN cards. VISITS starts at 41: ADD 1 to it. Then show:
DEAR WOZNIAK
ACCOUNT 004711
THIS IS VISIT 042
THANK YOU FOR BANKING WITH US.
cbc1-project.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. GREET.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.
cbc1-project.expectedOutput:
DEAR WOZNIAK
ACCOUNT 004711
THIS IS VISIT 042
THANK YOU FOR BANKING WITH US.

requirements.message: Count the visit with ADD 1 TO.

hints: 01 CUSTOMER PIC X(10). 01 ACCOUNT-NO PIC 9(6). 01 VISITS PIC 9(3) VALUE 41.
ACCEPT CUSTOMER. ACCEPT ACCOUNT-NO. ADD 1 TO VISITS.
DISPLAY "DEAR " CUSTOMER. and DISPLAY "ACCOUNT " ACCOUNT-NO. The PIC 9(6) adds the zeros by itself.

cb4.task:
Declare BALANCE as PIC S9(5)V99 with VALUE 120.50. ADD a deposit of 35.25, then ADD a withdrawal of -200.00. DISPLAY the balance after each step:
0015575
0004425-
cb4.starter:

       PROGRAM-ID. BALANCE.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.

ADD 35.25 TO BALANCE. DISPLAY BALANCE.
ADD -200.00 TO BALANCE. The S keeps the minus.

cb5.story: A payroll cheque from 1970: the amount must be safe from forgers.
cb5.task:
MOVE 1234.5 into a field with PIC $**,**9.99 and DISPLAY "PAY " and the field. Then MOVE -42.75 into a field with PIC $$$,$$9.99CR and DISPLAY "REFUND " and it:
PAY $*1,234.50
REFUND     $42.75CR
cb5.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CHEQUE.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.
hints: 01 CHEQUE-OUT PIC $**,**9.99.
01 REFUND-OUT PIC $$$,$$9.99CR.
MOVE 1234.5 TO CHEQUE-OUT. DISPLAY "PAY " CHEQUE-OUT.

cb6.title: The Customer Record
cb6.story: The bank keeps its customers in records. Build one, and print it as a report line.
cb6.task:
Make a group CUSTOMER with CUST-NAME PIC X(8), CUST-NO PIC 9(5) and CUST-BAL PIC 9(5)V99. Fill it with ADA, 42 and 1815.36. Then make a report line group: the name, a FILLER of 2 spaces, the number, a FILLER " BALANCE ", and the balance in PIC $$$,$$9.99. MOVE the fields into the line and DISPLAY it:
ADA       00042 BALANCE  $1,815.36
cb6.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. CUSTREC.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.

requirements.message: Use FILLER for the fixed parts.
Print the balance with a floating $.

hints: 01 CUSTOMER. 05 CUST-NAME PIC X(8). 05 CUST-NO PIC 9(5). 05 CUST-BAL PIC 9(5)V99.
01 CUST-LINE. 05 CL-NAME PIC X(8). 05 FILLER PIC X(2) VALUE SPACES. 05 CL-NO PIC 9(5). 05 FILLER PIC X(9) VALUE " BALANCE ". 05 CL-BAL PIC $$$,$$9.99.
MOVE CUST-NAME TO CL-NAME, and so on, then DISPLAY CUST-LINE.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.

cbc2-project.expectedOutput:
PAYSLIP FOR GRACE
SALARY   $2,150.75
BONUS      $125.50
TOTAL    $2,276.25

requirements.message: Print the amounts with a floating $.

hints: 01 PAY-LINE. 05 PL-LABEL PIC X(7). 05 PL-AMOUNT PIC $$$,$$9.99.

cb7.title: Split the Bill
cb7.story: Five friends at a restaurant in 1975. The bill is 87.40, plus a tip.
cb7.task:
MULTIPLY the bill 87.40 by 1.15 (a 15 % tip) GIVING the total, ROUNDED to cents. DIVIDE the total by 5 GIVING each person's share, ROUNDED. Show both in PIC $$$9.99:
TOTAL $100.51
EACH   $20.10
cb7.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. SPLIT.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.
hints: MULTIPLY BILL BY 1.15 GIVING TOTAL ROUNDED.
DIVIDE TOTAL BY 5 GIVING EACH ROUNDED.
MOVE TOTAL TO OUT. DISPLAY "TOTAL " OUT.

cb8.title: Compound Interest
cb8.story: Grandma puts 2,500 dollars into a savings account in 1970, at 6 % a year.
cb8.task:
With COMPUTE, work out the balance after 10 years with interest on interest: BALANCE * 1.06 ** 10, ROUNDED to cents. Show it, and the interest earned, in PIC $$$,$$9.99:
AFTER 10 YEARS  $4,477.12
INTEREST        $1,977.12
cb8.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. INTEREST.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.

requirements.message: Raise to the power of 10 with **.

hints: 01 START-BAL PIC 9(5)V99 VALUE 2500. 01 BALANCE PIC 9(5)V99.
COMPUTE BALANCE ROUNDED = START-BAL * 1.06 ** 10.
COMPUTE EARNED = BALANCE - START-BAL.

cb9.title: The Shipping Desk
cb9.story: A mail-order company in 1980 charges shipping by weight. Read the parcels from cards.
cb9.task:
Read three weights in kg (PIC 99V9) with ACCEPT. For each, use EVALUATE: below 2 kg costs 4.90, 2 to 9.9 kg costs 7.90, 10 kg and more costs 14.90. Show each weight and price, with the weight in PIC Z9.9 and the price in PIC $$9.99:
 1.5 KG  $4.90
 7.0 KG  $7.90
12.0 KG $14.90
cb9.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. SHIPPING.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.

requirements.message: Use WHEN OTHER for the heavy parcels.

hints: EVALUATE TRUE WHEN WEIGHT < 2 MOVE 4.90 TO PRICE WHEN WEIGHT < 10 MOVE 7.90 TO PRICE WHEN OTHER MOVE 14.90 TO PRICE END-EVALUATE.
MOVE WEIGHT TO W-OUT. MOVE PRICE TO P-OUT. DISPLAY W-OUT " KG " P-OUT.

cbc3-project.title: The Invoice
cbc3-project.story: 1984: the office supply company prints its invoices on the mainframe.
cbc3-project.task:
Read 3 items, each as two cards: the quantity (PIC 999) and the unit price (PIC 9(4)V99). Print a line for each: quantity in PIC ZZ9, " X ", price and line total in PIC $$,$$9.99. Then: subtotal; a discount of 10 % if the subtotal is 500 or more (else 0); 19 % tax on what's left, ROUNDED; and the total due:
 10 X     $4.50   $45.00
  2 X   $199.00  $398.00
  5 X    $12.80   $64.00
SUBTOTAL   $507.00
DISCOUNT    $50.70
TAX         $86.70
TOTAL DUE  $543.00
cbc3-project.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. INVOICE.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.

requirements.message: Decide the discount with IF or EVALUATE.

hints: For each item: ACCEPT QTY. ACCEPT PRICE. MULTIPLY QTY BY PRICE GIVING LINE-TOTAL. ADD LINE-TOTAL TO SUBTOTAL. Then MOVE into the line fields and DISPLAY.
IF SUBTOTAL >= 500 COMPUTE DISCOUNT ROUNDED = SUBTOTAL * 0.10 ELSE MOVE 0 TO DISCOUNT END-IF.
COMPUTE TAX ROUNDED = (SUBTOTAL - DISCOUNT) * 0.19. COMPUTE TOTAL-DUE = SUBTOTAL - DISCOUNT + TAX.

cb10.title: The Countdown
cb10.story: Mission control, 1969, wants a countdown printed by the mainframe.
cb10.task: Write the paragraphs MAIN, SHOW-NUMBER and LIFT-OFF. MAIN performs SHOW-NUMBER UNTIL the counter (starting at 5) is 0, then performs LIFT-OFF and stops. SHOW-NUMBER displays the counter as T-MINUS 5 and so on, then subtracts 1. LIFT-OFF shows LIFT OFF!
cb10.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. COUNTDN.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.
cb10.expectedOutput:
T-MINUS 5
T-MINUS 4
T-MINUS 3
T-MINUS 2
T-MINUS 1
LIFT OFF!

requirements.message: End the main paragraph with STOP RUN.

hints: 01 COUNTER PIC 9 VALUE 5.
MAIN: PERFORM SHOW-NUMBER UNTIL COUNTER = 0. PERFORM LIFT-OFF. STOP RUN.
SHOW-NUMBER: DISPLAY "T-MINUS " COUNTER. SUBTRACT 1 FROM COUNTER.

cb11.title: The Times Table
cb11.story: A school in 1972 prints times tables for its pupils on the university's mainframe.
cb11.task:
Print the times table for 7, from 1 to 5, with PERFORM VARYING. Each line looks like 1 X 7 = 7, with the result in PIC ZZ9:
1 X 7 =   7
2 X 7 =  14
3 X 7 =  21
4 X 7 =  28
5 X 7 =  35
cb11.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. TIMES7.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.
hints: 01 I PIC 9. 01 PRODUCT PIC ZZ9.
PERFORM VARYING I FROM 1 BY 1 UNTIL I > 5 … END-PERFORM.
COMPUTE PRODUCT = I * 7. DISPLAY I " X 7 = " PRODUCT.

In a PERFORM VARYING loop, print each month and its amount (PIC ZZ,ZZ9), add up the total and find the best month. Then print the total, the best month, and the average (ROUNDED, PIC ZZ,ZZ9):
JAN  1,200
FEB    950
MAR  1,810
APR    700
MAY  1,305
JUN  2,045
TOTAL  8,010
BEST MONTH JUN
AVERAGE  1,335

       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

JAN  1,200
FEB    950
MAR  1,810
APR    700
MAY  1,305
JUN  2,045
TOTAL  8,010

cb13.title: The City Filter
cb13.story: The London branch wants a file of its own customers.
cb13.task:
Read CUSTOMERS, and WRITE every customer whose city is LONDON into a new file LONDONERS (OPEN OUTPUT). Close both, then read LONDONERS back and DISPLAY each record's name, and how many there were:
ADA LOVELACE
1 IN LONDON
cb13.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. LONDON.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT CUST-FILE ASSIGN TO CUSTOMERS.
           SELECT LONDON-FILE ASSIGN TO LONDONERS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD CUST-FILE.
       01 CUST-REC.
          05 CUST-NO      PIC 9(5).
          05 CUST-NAME    PIC X(12).
          05 CUST-CITY    PIC X(10).
          05 CUST-BAL     PIC 9(5)V99.
       FD LONDON-FILE.
       01 LONDON-REC.
          05 L-NO         PIC 9(5).
          05 L-NAME       PIC X(12).
          05 FILLER       PIC X(17).
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.

requirements.message: Create the new file with OPEN OUTPUT.

hints: SELECT CUST-FILE ASSIGN TO CUSTOMERS. SELECT LONDON-FILE ASSIGN TO LONDONERS.
IF CUST-CITY = "LONDON" WRITE LONDON-REC FROM CUST-REC END-IF
Set the end flag back to "N" before reading the new file.

cb15.story: The sales manager wants one line per region: how many sales, and how much.
cb15.task:
Read SALES (sorted by region) with a control break. For each region, print its name, the number of sales and its total (count in PIC 9, total in PIC $$$,$$9.99), and at the end the grand total:
NORTH 3    $419.25
SOUTH 2    $195.25
WEST  1    $300.00
ALL   6    $914.50
cb15.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. BYREGION.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT SALES-FILE ASSIGN TO SALES.
       DATA DIVISION.

cbc5-project.title: The Bank Statement
cbc5-project.story: 1982: once a month, the bank prints a statement for every account. Build the job that does it, the way it really was done.
cbc5-project.task:
Read TRANS (account, D or W, amount; sorted by account) with a control break by account. For each account, print a line with the account number, deposits, withdrawals and the net change (net in PIC -$$,$$9.99, the others in PIC $$,$$9.99). At the end, print the number of transactions and the bank's net change:
00007   $100.00    $25.50    $74.50
00042   $500.00   $129.99   $370.01
01959    $10.00     $0.00    $10.00
TRANSACTIONS 6
BANK NET    $454.51
cbc5-project.starter:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. STATEMNT.
       ENVIRONMENT DIVISION.
       INPUT-OUTPUT SECTION.
       FILE-CONTROL.
           SELECT TRANS-FILE ASSIGN TO TRANS.
       DATA DIVISION.
       FILE SECTION.
       FD TRANS-FILE.
       01 TRANS-REC.
          05 T-ACCOUNT    PIC 9(5).
          05 T-TYPE       PIC X.
          05 T-AMOUNT     PIC 9(5)V99.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.

       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
           
           STOP RUN.

requirements.message: Notice the account changes with a previous key.
The net change needs a signed field (S).

hints: 01 STMT-LINE. 05 SL-ACCT PIC 9(5). 05 SL-DEP PIC $$,$$9.99. 05 SL-WDR PIC $$,$$9.99. 05 SL-NET PIC -$$,$$9.99. (Mind the spaces.)
For each record: IF T-TYPE = "D" ADD T-AMOUNT TO DEPOSITS ELSE ADD T-AMOUNT TO WITHDRAWALS END-IF.
At a break: COMPUTE NET = DEPOSITS - WITHDRAWALS, print the line, ADD NET TO BANK-NET, reset the account totals.
